question: Does three times the baseline learning budget improve recovery at the corrected chest-first dose on both seeds?
decision: Change only the Stage 7 update budget from 100 to 300 per arm; retain the original reward mixture and root-velocity scale 1. Evaluate all four endpoints on both impact levels/directions/backends (256 cases). An arm qualifies for fresh 120-second Stand only if both seeds show strict target-dose gain over their source, no direction/level regression, all hits Chest-first without Head, and backend admission. Assess each qualifying arm on both seeds/backends (32 additional cases per qualifying arm, maximum 320 total). Report replicated absolute recipe improvement separately from impact-practice improvement over matched quiet controls. Unassessed Stand is null, never a pass. No automatic promotion.
reuse: Verified source 120-second Stand from the earlier pilot and frozen impact baselines from Stages 3 and 5; actor identity must match. These are not new evaluation cases.
rationale: Stages 11 and 12 fail replicated improvement from reward changes. Stage 13 shows that earlier launches change difficulty. Return to the Stage 7 reward and five-second launch, changing only the optimization budget from 100 to 300 updates per arm. Prior historical 300-update training used head-first 0.65 m launches and cannot answer whether longer learning helps at the corrected 0.25 m geometry. Use original full parents and fresh matched optimizers; preserve checkpoints at 100, 200 and 300 for a potential follow-up learning-curve assessment.
